releases.name: opencode-cordon 0.1.2 - clearer README & assets
releases.body:
Presentation release. No behaviour change to the policy engine.

## What changed
- README (English root, Chinese in `docs/`) rewritten around: the problem, a live 2.2.5 regression, how it works, verification, and what it is not.
- New assets: banner, architecture diagram, a real audit-report screenshot from the live session, and a social-preview image.
- CI now asserts the deny exit code instead of treating a correct deny as a failure; the badge is green.
- npm package page now uses the English root README.

## Install
```
opencode plugin add opencode-cordon
npx opencode-cordon init
```

Verified on OpenCode 2.2.5: `.env` read tightened ask -> deny, `rm -rf` tightened allow -> deny under `--auto`, both audited.

releases.name: opencode-cordon 0.1.0
releases.body:
First public release: a declarative permission cordon with an audit trail for OpenCode 2.

## Highlights
- JSONC policy with relaxed / balanced / strict presets; glob matching on action, tool, path, command and agent.
- permission.evaluate hook that only tightens: deny always wins, ask upgrades an allow, allow/no-match never touches the native decision.
- Append-only JSONL audit log (secrets redacted, commands hashed) plus a self-contained HTML report.
- CLI: check / evaluate / audit / init / redact. Zero runtime dependencies, Node >= 20.
- 57 tests, including a plugin adapter suite that drives the real @opencode/plugin hooks.

## Verified
Live regression on OpenCode 2.2.5 with --auto: .env read tightened ask -> deny, rm -rf ./scratch tightened allow -> deny, both recorded in the audit log, target file survived. See docs/REGRESSION.md.

## Install
`
opencode plugin add opencode-cordon
npx opencode-cordon init
`

Requires OpenCode 2.2.x. Not a sandbox; not an LLM reviewer; not a V1 compatibility layer.
